description: Open an objective dispute against a counter-signed receipt as the PAYER (the configured key must be the receipt payer). Reasons: not_delivered, wrong_content, duplicate_charge. Recording only: the ledger records your signed claim and opens an evidence window; it moves no money. The ledger opens a dispute only with room reserved in its dispute capacity for the claim, its triage and each party's first evidence item, the same on every plan; while that capacity is full it opens none (HTTP 503). adjudicate_dispute later runs deterministic triage on it, which classifies a duplicate_charge from the ledger's own receipts only when the disputed receipt carries a settlement transaction hash in 0x-prefixed 64-hex-digit form (either letter case), and escalates it otherwise; classifies an unanswered claim from the seller's silence; and marks anything else escalated, for an external venue the parties choose. Triage's duplicate_charge rule, R1, reads receipts from one seller to one payer that share one settlement transaction as one payment.

claimAmount.description: amount claimed back, as a decimal STRING in the receipt's settlement currency, e.g. "12.50". The ledger records it as stated and checks it against no payment; a refund triage result logs this amount as a pending refund entry

reason.description: grounds: 'not_delivered' nothing arrived · 'wrong_content' delivered but not what was bought · 'duplicate_charge' the same supply was billed twice (classified by triage from the ledger's own receipts only when the disputed receipt carries a settlement transaction hash in 0x-prefixed 64-hex-digit form (either letter case), and escalated otherwise; no party evidence is read; R1, the rule that classifies it, reads receipts from one seller to one payer that share one settlement transaction as one payment)

receiptDigest.description: 0x-prefixed keccak256 digest of the counter-signed receipt being disputed

statement.description: for humans reading the record — never an input to the triage rules
